rv.q: "Spamalot" has a boisterous energy that appropriately evokes the idea of naughty schoolboys running riot with a budget.

It seems safe to say that such a good time is being had by so many people (including the cast) at the Shubert Theater that this fitful, eager celebration of inanity will find a large and lucrative audience among those who value the virtues of shrewd idiocy, artful tackiness and wide-eyed impiety.
Yes, indeed, we enthusiastically endorse Spamalot, an outrageously silly show and witty spoof, which will most assuredly entertain young as well as old.
It is like- able - but not a blockbuster

cn.t: Critics enthusiastically embrace this crowd-pleasing adaptation of "Monty Python and the Holy Grail," praising its polished production and talented cast led by Tim Curry, Hank Azaria, and David Hyde Pierce.

vs.sum: The Shubert Theatre offers good sightlines with minimal obstructions, though some seats may require leaning forward for a full view. The sound quality is generally consistent and clear. While legroom is limited in some areas, the theater's historic charm and central location add to its appeal. Facilities are average, with typical lines at restrooms and concessions.

acc.note: 7 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. No wheelchair-accessible restrooms (available across street).
